titulo: Redict deprecated in favor of Valkey
resumo: Drew DeVault has announced that Redict , a fork of Redis that was created in response to Redis's 2024 license change , has been deprecated. He recommends switching to Valkey , the permissively licensed Redis fork supported by the Linux Foundation. The two projects are mutually compatible, so switching should be as simple as changing which package is installed and renaming the configuration file. I had hoped to rally the Redis diaspora around a copyleft initiative, to protect ourselves from future rug-pulls, and made Redict to serve this purpose. However, with the valkey project's success, and Redis's return to a copyleft license, Redict was not able to build a sustainable community. titulo: Brain connectivity in high-traffic regions may shape how multiple sclerosis damages tissue
resumo: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disorder in which the immune system mistakenly turns against the body's own cells. In this case, immune cells attack myelin, a fatty, protein-rich substance that forms a protective coating around nerve fibers. Myelin gives the brain's white matter its characteristic whitish appearance and helps nerve cells communicate with one another. However, the damage does not stop there. MS is also linked to the gradual shrinking or atrophy of gray matter, the brain tissue where most nerve cell bodies are found. As this tissue shrinks, people tend to experience more severe symptoms, including difficulties with movement and thinking.

resumo: A woodcock is an odd little bird with a long, skinny bill and a plump, chunky body that's shaped like an American football. It mostly hangs out near the ground, but it does a mating display in which it makes a buzzy, tweeting call and then takes off zigzagging across the sky. The woodcock stands out from most of the members of its family, the sandpipers. The majority of sandpiper species are champion migrators that traverse thousands of miles every year, but many woodcock species and their closest cousins, the snipes, have evolved to migrate shorter distances. Some island-dwelling species of woodcocks and snipes don't migrate at all.

titulo: These Engineers Are Cleaning Up Connected Cars’ Security Flaws
resumo: Today’s connected vehicles collect and transmit far more personal data from drivers and passengers than their predecessors, with costly consequences. The Center for Automotive Management in Germany estimates that cyberattacks have caused more than $20 billion in damage to the auto industry as of 2025, twenty times higher than in 2022. This week, engineers and cybersecurity researchers are gathering in Bonn, Germany, for the Embedded Security in Cars (escar) conference to discuss using AI for defense, hardening chips, and otherwise securing the auto industry’s data handling.
